investigated_reserve.portfolio_decision: Not counted as an additional final task. Root retains only Chefman handle and Oster ring from food branch. No independent strong second extension met threshold.

importance.person: Household cook replacing blender lid after filling or washing
importance.real_outcome: Broad lid correctly seated and captured against lift before appliance use
importance.why_it_matters: Recognizable household blender preparation, with two separable user-facing operations: lid seating and handle-driven locking. No niche repair, no borrowed occupation totals.
importance.strict_objection: Many households know blender lids firsthand; fewer use this exact locking-handle model. Importance is plausible but not independently proved by familiar object alone.

investigated_reserve.instruction: Put the lid on the pitcher with its handle upright, align the arrows and fully seat the rim. Fold the locking handle down so the latches catch beneath the pitcher tabs. Leave the pour-spout cap closed and both hands clear.
investigated_reserve.core_ability: Mechanically coupled lid seating and handle-actuated under-tab capture. No bayonet yaw motion, no over-center force-peak assumption, no success-on-pose latch flag.
investigated_reserve.bimanual_requirement: Useful but not claimed intrinsically mandatory: one hand may stabilize pitcher by its original handle while the other acquires lid and folds handle. A heavy original base may permit some one-arm solutions; do not manufacture a two-hand requirement.

verified_topology: Detachable lid seats with handle raised
Handle rotates down on a visible hinge
Lid latch elements end beneath pitcher tabs and resist lid lift
permissible_bounded_engineering: Smooth unimportant shell details, approximate lumped masses and friction disclosed
Conservative scale range for outer lid/pitcher/handle envelope, tied to2.1L product drawings; do not label nominal values OEM dimensions

A causal representative contact linkage may support a CPU planning experiment if clearly labeled, with actual latch/tab interference and passive retention. It is not automatically faithful to unknown hidden OEM cam geometry.
forbidden: Attaching lid when center/yaw is near target
Turning off lid/pitcher collisions to permit assembly
Using handle angle alone as evidence of retention
Inventing an over-center spring because swing-top competitor has one
Transferring newerBN700C anti-fold interlock behavior toBL610 without revision-specific proof

physical_scoring.initial: Detached original lid, handle raised, pour cap shut; dry pitcher/base/blade already in normal state, power unplugged.
physical_scoring.partial: 0.5 if lid correctly oriented and fully rim-seated with handle still raised, no robot support for2s; otherwise0 until an independently stable stage exists. A proposed2mm rim gap is an authored benchmark threshold to validate against actual hardware, not OEM tolerance.
physical_scoring.full: 1.0 requires full rim seating, handle in original closed detent, every matching latch captured beneath its pitcher tab, pour cap shut, both hands at least50mm clear2s. Evaluator holds pitcher body and gently attempts to lift lid at its rigid edges without touching release/handle: lid remains retained. Then OEM release allows normal removal to prove it is not wedged. Pull-force limit must be chosen from measured original behavior; no fabricated manufacturer torque/force.
physical_scoring.measurement: Ruler/side photos for rim height and handle posture, transparent-pitcher views for accessible latch overlap, and manual edge-lift/release check. Do not demand invisible internal flags or use a powered motor test as retention proxy.
physical_scoring.invalid_damage: Broken/bent catches, cracked lid/pitcher, forced rim wedging, added glue/ties, destructive blade contact or powered motor invalidates score.

wrong_solutions_prevented.wrong: Close handle while lid stands on rim or wrong corner
wrong_solutions_prevented.prevention: Correct arrow/spout orientation, rim height and edge-lift retention required.

wrong_solutions_prevented.wrong: Rest lid correctly but never actuate catches
wrong_solutions_prevented.prevention: Physical under-tab capture plus independent released retention check.

wrong_solutions_prevented.wrong: Press lid down with gripper throughout endpoint
wrong_solutions_prevented.prevention: 50mm hands-clear interval and evaluator proof after release.

wrong_solutions_prevented.wrong: Trap lid by force/wedge instead of latches
wrong_solutions_prevented.prevention: Damage check and normal OEM release/removal path must remain possible.

wrong_solutions_prevented.wrong: Only move handle to a geometric target
wrong_solutions_prevented.prevention: Handle posture alone receives no full credit; catches must physically resist edge lift.

physical_scoring.reset: With machine unplugged, press original release and lift handle, remove lid normally, return detached lid and original pitcher/base to fixed counter poses. No consumables.

closest_official_competitors.head: c82d718b83f44a49ed9e7bdb2a49d8434563e103
closest_official_competitors.semantic_comparison: Actual task seats a separate stopper then moves a neck-mounted wire-bail lever through an over-center peak to clamp a bottle. Its task.py/bottlekit.py scorer requires past-center with stopper seated and released upright bottle. Ninja has one detachable broad lid and a central hinged handle actuating latches under pitcher tabs; source does NOT establish over-center peak. Same general close-then-lever pattern is insufficient by itself, but setting/outcome closeness remains a novelty concern.

closest_official_competitors.head: c82d718b83f44a49ed9e7bdb2a49d8434563e103
closest_official_competitors.semantic_comparison: Actual bottle opening requires releasing a U safety loop, pressing a spring-return rocker hook and allowing hinged lid to spring open. Native contact hooks/loop and lid/rocker springs plus angle/upright scoring were read. Ninja closes a detached lid by folding a single handle; no independent safety loop and no opening a spring-hinged lid.

closest_official_competitors.head: c82d718b83f44a49ed9e7bdb2a49d8434563e103
closest_official_competitors.semantic_comparison: Actual rigid enclosure lid has two independent opposed spring sliders 20cm apart. Robot must retract both simultaneously while lifting; score counts one/both release, elevation and placed lid. Ninja couples lid catches to one central handle. Different coordination and source equipment, though both rely on lid catch/slot retention.

closest_official_competitors.head: c82d718b83f44a49ed9e7bdb2a49d8434563e103
closest_official_competitors.semantic_comparison: Actual snap-case closure presses flexural corner catches and scores released retained lid. Ninja must move a separate operating lever after seating; snapping lid down alone is insufficient. Mechanical retention still must be implemented physically, not granted on handle pose.

external_benchmark_audit.actual_overlap: Same model091 has10 open-planning Task2 and7 next-action Task4 definitions; some explicitly include close(lid). Thus same object and endpoint already appear. Do NOT claim external endpoint absent.
external_benchmark_audit.ability_distinction: Read benchmark definitions ask for strings from atomic actions such as pick/close/rotate; source model091gt_part exposes lid and controls, not separate operating handle/catches. The proposed task would test continuous physical acquisition, handle motion and passive retained contact. This is a potentially meaningful distinction, not a proved official novelty clearance.
external_benchmark_audit.hard_limit: If evaluator regards this same familiar blender-lid closure as the same physical skill despite planning-versus-execution distinction, novelty fails. Portfolio omits Ninja rather than assume acceptance.

yam.status: PLANNING ONLY, no executed CPU, IK, reach, collision, grip-force or mechanism test.315 collision hulls per arm remain required.
yam.grasp: Pitcher loop/vertical bar for stabilizing hand; lid acquisition at original rim/pour-cap-free corner or raised handle only if its dynamics permit; folding stroke by original broad handle, no added tabs.93.9mm nominal jaw aperture does not prove purchase.
critical_paths: Approach detached lid without forcing handle to rotate
Orient lid/spout above rim and descend past installed blade shaft
Release/regrasp if needed and sweep locking handle from upright to flat
Withdraw working fingers without opening pour cap or release button
risks: Palm under lid rim can hit pitcher before finger contacts settle
Working wrist and bracing hand collide around handle corner
Blade shaft/upper blade and lid underside must remain collision-active
Raised handle and release button leave limited safe purchase
No verified spring/cam reaction torque, contact clearance or original component mass

bounded_cpu_preflight_plan_not_run.purpose: Determine access sensitivity for the known user-facing topology, without pretending OEM internal CAD or full clearance certification.
bounded_cpu_preflight_plan_not_run.geometry: Parameterize outer pitcher/lid/handle dimensions over source-proportion-consistent ranges; retain full installed blade/base obstacles and native robot hulls. Treat actual latch/tab contact envelope as unresolved local mechanism; do not weld lid.
observables: Second-arm clearance while stabilizing original pitcher handle
Reachable raised-to-flat handle sweep without forbidden collision
Whether feasible solutions survive outer-envelope and handle-width perturbation
bounded_cpu_preflight_plan_not_run.interpretation: Successful bounded access cases only justify continued source/geometry work, not a verified product path or physics implementation. A collision across all plausible original-scale cases cheaply kills the candidate. Root did not select this for final CPU run.

essential_missing_inputs: Actual number/placement and motion path ofBL610 latch elements, hidden handle linkage and detent/release coupling
Safe physical lid acquisition site at stock-YAM scale and actual masses
Resolution of same-model external close(lid) novelty objection
investigated_reserve.cheapest_falsifier: First reject under strict same-model external endpoint novelty if physical-versus-planning distinction is judged insufficient. Otherwise run bounded full-hull lid/handle approach and fold sweep; reject if no grasp survives plausible original-size envelopes. Exact OEM cam CAD is not required merely to run this bounded screen.
investigated_reserve.relative_effort: Medium rigid mechanism if hidden linkage is authentically resolved; larger novelty risk than Chefman handle or Oster retaining ring.

critic.strongest_rejection: Same Ninja close(lid) appears in existing external benchmark; accepted swing-top/dual-latch/snap-case tasks already cover close/lever/latch outcomes.
critic.resolution: Actual mechanics differ from bayonet, wire-bail over-center and independent dual sliders. External measured ability is atomic-action planning. This supports a distinction but does not settle novelty; remains reserve.

root_reconciliation: Original food_warehouse ledger source-gated labels are preserved. Root may justify bounded CPU preflight for Chefman/Oster from established essential topology and disclosed parameter ranges; that is a finite planning/contact test, not authenticated OEM geometry, verified YAM clearance or demonstrated task success.
no_execution: No task implementation, CPU test, GPU/model run, submission, purchase, commit or push performed.
